items.name: Spec Compliance
items.note: mark_status now returns (previous, item, to_outbox); all four CLI writers (dismiss, snooze, amend, promote/defer/unpark) print the outbox note plus its converse (tracked-from-a-non-default-branch) in both --json and human modes; webui _emit_result carries an additive route key. Deliberately did NOT turn the derivation into a caller flag. Scope grew beyond the brief's literal two-call-site ask (dismiss --json, snooze) to also cover triage_promote.py's promote()/_transition() and the CLI's cmd_promote/_status_flip dispatcher, after two independent external reviewers (GLM, OpenAI/Codex) flagged that dismiss's non-json path was silent — the same 'silence should never be the report' rationale the brief itself states.

items.name: Error Handling
items.note: route_note() wraps its git branch lookups in try/except and returns None on failure — advisory only, never blocks or changes the CLI's exit code.

items.name: Security Basics
items.note: No user input reaches SQL/HTML. Branch name is shown via repr(); git ref-name rules already forbid control characters, so no injection/console-encoding risk — consistent with this file's existing (unhardened) stderr writes.

items.name: Test Quality
items.note: test_triage_route_report.py + test_triage_route_report_dispatch.py (split to stay under the 300-LOC guideline) assert observable outcomes only: 3-tuple values, JSON route key, exact stderr note text. Covers outbox + tracked-branch for all four writers, a 3-tuple index-stability regression guard, a show-has-no-route-key negative case, and the negative tracked-on-default-branch/no-origin case a spec-reviewer flagged as missing. A Stage-1 spec-reviewer pass on the scope-extended diff also caught a real regression (unconditional 'route' key broke 4 pre-existing exact-dict-equality tests in test_triage_promote.py/test_triage_defer.py) — fixed by updating those 4 assertions, re-verified 66/66 passing.

items.name: Performance Basics
items.note: No loops/N+1. route_note's two extra git subprocess calls happen once per CLI invocation, only on the human (non-json) output path.

items.name: Naming & Structure
items.note: Extracted lib/triage_route.py to hold triage_cli_commands.py at or under its existing 324-line bloat-baseline budget (currently 320; would otherwise have ratcheted it). triage_promote.py stays at 416/420. Both confirmed via the anti-ratchet hook, which passes clean.

items.name: Affected Boundaries
items.note: Producer/consumer: CLI --json stdout (producer) -> WebUI Command Center (consumer, external repo). Producer-side round-trip probed via subprocess CLI invocation in the new test modules (both to_outbox branches, all four writers). Consumer can't be round-tripped from this repo; change is purely additive (new optional route key), so existing JSON.parse-based consumers are unaffected. Not touches_io_boundary-flagged: no .env*/hooks.json/settings.json/*_config.json/*_state.json touched, and no new anchored json.dump/load producer+consumer pair — only an additive key on an already-existing, already-tested json.dumps call.
